verdict.rationale: Letta's chat interfaces (CLI, chat.letta.com, desktop/web app) are fundamentally conversational, and features like /remember explicitly accept free-form natural-language instructions (e.g., 'always use pnpm in this repo') to steer agent behavior. However, most operational controls (fork, pin, doctor, agents list, shared-memory create, headless flags) are structured slash-commands/CLI flags rather than natural-language commands, so NL control is limited to teaching/memory rather than full product operation. Missing for 10: evidence that broader agent/system operations (deployment, config, environment switching) can be driven by plain NL rather than explicit commands, and independent confirmation of NL-driven control working reliably.
